recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further wording about how outcome and contributedToDeath relate should wait for a new Patient Care decision rather than being added under FHIR-18857.
issue_request: FHIR-18857 was Published / Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to add FamilyMemberHistory.condition.contributedToDeath 0..1 boolean with death-contribution semantics, delete the old FamilyMemberHistory.condition comment that inferred no primary cause of death from absent death outcomes, and update FamilyMemberHistory.condition.outcome to indicate what happened following the condition with death date captured on the relation.
initial_application: The Jira snapshot identifies commit 04c4d675c5f4. That commit cites GF#18857 and updates FamilyMemberHistory material, including adding contributedToDeath in the example and changing the older spreadsheet source. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d5 carried the approved outcome definition and contributedToDeath element into the current StructureDefinition XML source.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists familymemberhistory as an active core resource and assigns it to Patient Care, confirming current build scope. FHIR-17808 later reused the same outcome/contributedToDeath pattern for FamilyMemberHistory.procedure, and FHIR-47829 later added summary flags to condition and condition.code without changing the FHIR-18857 death-contribution semantics. A 2025 implementers Zulip thread discusses outcome versus contributedToDeath usage, but no formal contrary Confluence or Jira decision was found.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current StructureDefinition has FamilyMemberHistory.condition.outcome with the approved definition and FamilyMemberHistory.condition.contributedToDeath as a 0..1 boolean; the example uses contributedToDeath; and source search found no remaining old condition comment about absent outcomes implying no primary cause of death. The current definition uses the real element name contributedToDeath where the Jira resolution appears to have said causeOfDeath by mistake, preserving the intended meaning.
